label: cdp:st:C.2.VII.1
reason: Root independently wrote the exact torsion-power meromorphic-function argument before reading the target step. Replace only the extra Gauduchon-degree ending by that completed preread argument; no theorem statement or other proof step changed.
old_paragraph:
For any Gauduchon metric
$\omega$, the degree of $\OO(C)$ is
$\int_C\omega>0$, whereas a torsion line has degree
zero. Hence $k=1$.
new_paragraph:
Choose $n>0$ trivializing $\OO((k-1)C)^{\otimes n}$.
A trivialization compared with the canonical meromorphic
section gives a meromorphic function with divisor
$n(k-1)C$. For $k>1$ it has no poles and a nonzero
effective zero divisor, impossible on the compact
connected surface. For $k=0$ its reciprocal has that
property. Hence $k=1$.
